data.hypothesis: A CTA can reuse each staged source-particle tile across its active target threads, reducing repeated global source loads while retaining the original interaction order and exactly one target per thread. Shared storage is 256 particles (7,168 bytes); staging and synchronization overhead may outweigh reuse for some sizes, so performance remains to be measured.
data.notes: The baseline is valid and measured at a mean of 0.001844410 seconds; no candidate measurement is available yet. The kernel keeps inactive output lanes participating in every barrier, stages partial final tiles safely, and preserves the per-target source iteration order. The configured shared-memory allocation is 7,168 bytes for 256 seven-float particles; target-specific acceptance and performance are for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Use one target particle per thread and retain the existing 256-thread block mapping.
Stage up to 256 source particles at a time in dynamically allocated shared memory, reusing each tile across active target threads.
Use block-wide barriers around tile consumption; handle partial source tiles and suppress out-of-range outputs.
Set launch shared-memory allocation to 7,168 bytes for a full tile.
